analysis_title: DAXDA Next-Gen Geometric & Crystallographic Mapping of Mars Biosignatures & Habitability Nodes

areoid_planetary_geometry.reference_datum: MOLA Areoid (Mean Volumetric Radius 3,389.5 km; Equatorial 3,396.2 km; Polar 3,376.2 km)
areoid_planetary_geometry.dichotomy_great_circle_law: The five primary equatorial/mid-latitude organic & biosignature targets — Jezero ('Cheyava Falls'), Nili Fossae, Gale ('Cumberland' alkanes), Gusev ('Home Plate' silica), and Mawrth/Oxia Planum — all lie along a single Great Circle inclined ~28.5° to the Martian equator (pole at 61.5°N, 15.0°E) within an elevation band of -1,940 m to -4,450 m MOLA. Geometrically, this ring is the equipotential paleo-coastline where Noachian river deltas and hydrothermal fracture systems emptied into the Northern Oceanus Borealis.

polyhedral_and_crystallographic_harmonic.match_to_tetrahedral_icosahedral_angle: Matches the 108° dodecahedral pentagon angle and 109.47° tetrahedral SiO4 / Ice Ih / Greigite bond angle within 1.0°.
polyhedral_and_crystallographic_harmonic.match_to_fcc_spinel_octahedral_angle: Matches the 70.53° {111} octahedral dihedral angle of Greigite (Fe3S4) and Magnetite (Fe3O4).

crystallographic_biosignature_triad.1_redox_spinels_and_phosphates: Greigite (Fe3S4, Fd-3m, 70.53°/109.47°) + Vivianite (Fe3(PO4)2·8H2O, C2/m) — electron-transfer mineral rims around organic carbon ('Cheyava Falls' leopard spots).
crystallographic_biosignature_triad.2_hexagonal_clay_shields: Smectite Phyllosilicates (Nontronite/Saponite/Montmorillonite, 60°/120° hexagonal siloxane sheets) — catalytic polymerization templates & radiation shields for C10–C12 fatty-acid chains ('Cumberland' mudstone).
crystallographic_biosignature_triad.3_cryosphere_ice_ih_and_silica_tetrahedr: Hexagonal Water Ice Ih (P6_3/mmc, 60°/109.47°) & Opal-A Silica (SiO2·nH2O, 109.47° SiO4 tetrahedra) — entombing hydrothermal hot-spring sinters ('Home Plate') and subglacial brine reservoirs (Ultimi Scopuli).

mapped_biosignature_sites.name: Jezero Crater — Bright Angel ('Cheyava Falls' Rock, Neretva Vallis)
key_detections: Millimeter-scale 'leopard spots' with dark Fe-phosphate (Vivianite) & Fe-sulfide (Greigite) reaction rims
SHERLOC UV Raman G-band organic carbon co-located inside redox-spotted mudstone
Crosscutting white calcium-sulfate (Bassanite/Gypsum) aqueous veins in ancient river delta inlet

host_mineral_crystallography.space_groups: Fd-3m (227, Cubic Inverse Spinel) & C2/m (12, Monoclinic)
host_mineral_crystallography.lattice_role: Greigite crystallizes in the cubic inverse-spinel Oh lattice with 70.53° octahedral and 109.47° tetrahedral Fe-S coordination — on Earth, low-temperature Fe3+/SO4^2- reduction into greigite + vivianite halos around organic carbon is driven by sulfate- and iron-reducing bacteria.

mapped_biosignature_sites.planetary_geometric_alignment: Sits directly on the -2,540 m Oceanus Borealis paleo-shoreline equipotential ring at the western concentric fault rim of the Isidis Impact Basin (70.5° conjugate shear intersection with Nili Fossae).
mapped_biosignature_sites.earth_analog: Lake Salda Hydromagnesite Delta (Turkey) & Reducing Proterozoic Lacustrine Redbeds

mapped_biosignature_sites.name: Gale Crater — Yellowknife Bay ('Cumberland' Mudstone) & Mount Sharp
key_detections: Long-chain linear alkanes: decane (C10H22), undecane (C11H24), and dodecane (C12H26) from fatty-acid precursors (2025)
Thiophenes (C4H4S), chlorobenzene, and strongly depleted carbon-13 isotopes (delta-13C down to -137 permil)
Seasonal background atmospheric methane (CH4) cycle (0.41 ppbv winter to 0.65 ppbv summer, with spikes to 21 ppbv)

host_mineral_crystallography.primary_minerals: Ferrian Saponite / Nontronite (2:1 Smectite Clay) + Magnetite (Fe3O4)
host_mineral_crystallography.lattice_role: Hexagonal 60°/120° SiO4 tetrahedral sheets sandwiching octahedral Fe/Mg layers create negatively charged interlayer galleries (~10–14 Å d-spacing) that bind and shield long-chain organic acids from ionizing radiation.

mapped_biosignature_sites.planetary_geometric_alignment: Occupies the exact equatorial inflection node of the 28.5°-inclined Martian Hemispheric Dichotomy Great Circle, 37° SW of the Elysium volcanic rise.
mapped_biosignature_sites.earth_analog: Pilbara Craton 3.5 Ga Lacustrine Shales (Western Australia) & Antarctic Dry Valley Paleolakes

mapped_biosignature_sites.name: Gusev Crater — Columbia Hills ('Home Plate' Opalline Silica Nodules)
key_detections: ~90 wt% pure Opal-A amorphous/nanocrystalline hydrated silica (SiO2·nH2O)
Finger-like (digitate), nodular, millimeter-branched sinter structures with hollow central conduits
Adjacent hydrothermal sulfate-rich fumarolic soils and basaltic tuff

host_mineral_crystallography.lattice_role: Rapid cooling of silica-saturated hydrothermal spring waters polymerizes 109.47° SiO4 tetrahedra into colloidal nanospheres that entomb and fossilize biofilm filaments.

mapped_biosignature_sites.planetary_geometric_alignment: Aligned along the eastern Dichotomy Great Circle arc at the mouth of Ma'adim Vallis (one of Mars's largest outflow channels, draining the Southern Highlands into the Northern Lowlands).
mapped_biosignature_sites.earth_analog: El Tatio High-Altitude Geyser Field (Atacama Desert, Chile, 4,320 m ASL)

mapped_biosignature_sites.name: Nili Fossae — Carbonate-Serpentine & Methane Graben Corridor
mapped_biosignature_sites.mission_and_year: MRO CRISM / Mars Express PFS & ExoMars TGO (2008–2024)
key_detections: Extensive Mg-carbonate (Magnesite), Serpentine ((Mg,Fe)3Si2O5(OH)4), and Fe/Mg-smectite exposures
Olivine-rich Noachian crust fractured by concentric Isidis grabens enabling deep water-rock serpentinization
Regional focus of episodic orbital methane (CH4) plume reports during northern summer

host_mineral_crystallography.space_groups: P31m / Cm (Trigonal-Monoclinic) & R-3c (167, Trigonal Calcite Group)
host_mineral_crystallography.lattice_role: Serpentinization oxidizes ferrous Fe2+ in olivine to ferric Fe3+ in magnetite (Oh, 70.53°), releasing molecular H2 gas that reduces dissolved CO2 (in trigonal 120° carbonate) into abiotic or biotic methane (CH4).

mapped_biosignature_sites.planetary_geometric_alignment: Concentric graben arc tangential to Isidis Planitia impact ring, striking 045°–060° in exact hexagonal/Riedel shear alignment with Jezero Crater 3.5° to the southeast.
mapped_biosignature_sites.earth_analog: Lost City Hydrothermal Field (Mid-Atlantic Ridge) & Samail Ophiolite (Oman)

mapped_biosignature_sites.name: Mawrth Vallis & Oxia Planum — Stratified Phyllosilicate Paleosol Horizon
mapped_biosignature_sites.mission_and_year: MRO CRISM / ESA ExoMars Rosalind Franklin Landing Zone
key_detections: >200 m thick finely laminated sequence of Noachian Fe/Mg-smectite clays capped by Al-clays (Kaolinite/Montmorillonite)
Ferrous (Fe2+) to ferric (Fe3+) redox weathering profile + hydrated sulfates (Jarosite/Bassanite)
Wide deltaic fan and standing-water basin emptying into Chryse Planitia paleo-ocean

host_mineral_crystallography.lattice_role: High surface-area (~800 m2/g) hexagonal phyllosilicate basal planes act as catalytic templates for RNA/peptide polymerization (Ferris montmorillonite catalysis) and long-term organic preservation.

mapped_biosignature_sites.planetary_geometric_alignment: Northernmost vertex of the Dichotomy Great Circle in the Western Hemisphere, directly opposite Gale/Gusev (156°–180° antipodal chord across Chryse Planitia).

mapped_biosignature_sites.name: Eridania Basin — Deep-Sea Alkaline Hydrothermal Vent Deposits
mapped_biosignature_sites.mission_and_year: MRO CRISM & MGS MOLA Bathymetric Reconstruction (2017–2023)
key_detections: 400 m thick deep-water hydrothermal mineral assemblage: saponite, talc, serpentine, and Fe-rich mica (glauconite)
Paleo-sea basin once holding ~210,000 km3 of water (9x all North American Great Lakes combined) at 1,000–1,500 m depth
Deep-crustal remanent magnetic anomalies (Mars Global Surveyor MAG) overlying the basin floor

host_mineral_crystallography.lattice_role: Submarine volcanism heated mineral-rich alkaline fluids at the bottom of a deep ice-covered sea, forming Fe-S and Ni-Fe mineral membranes with natural proton (pH) gradients identical to Earth's earliest origin-of-life vents.

mapped_biosignature_sites.planetary_geometric_alignment: Occupies the Southern Hemisphere Icosahedral-Dodecahedral Vertex in Terra Sirenum / Cimmeria, where Mars's strongest ancient crustal magnetic stripes (>1,500 nT) intersect.
mapped_biosignature_sites.earth_analog: Archean Isua / Nuvvuagittuq Submarine Hydrothermal Vent Complexes

mapped_biosignature_sites.name: Ultimi Scopuli (South Polar Layered Deposits) — Basal Radar Anomaly
mapped_biosignature_sites.mission_and_year: ESA Mars Express MARSIS Subsurface Radar (2018–2024)
key_detections: High-permittivity 20 km wide basal radar reflection 1.5 km beneath the South Polar Ice Cap
Interpreted as hypersaline Ca/Mg-perchlorate liquid brine pocket or hydrated smectite clay/brine mud layer
Overlain by stratified hexagonal Water Ice (Ih) and seasonal cubic Dry Ice (CO2, Pa-3)

host_mineral_crystallography.primary_minerals: Hexagonal Ice Ih (H2O) + Mg(ClO4)2·6H2O Brine / Smectite
host_mineral_crystallography.lattice_role: Perchlorate tetrahedral anions (ClO4^-, 109.47°) disrupt the hexagonal hydrogen-bond network of Ice Ih, depressing the freezing point of water down to -70°C and creating potential subglacial brine habitats.

mapped_biosignature_sites.planetary_geometric_alignment: Anchors the South Polar rotational axis (-81°S), directly analogous to Antarctica's Lake Vostok (-78.46°S) and Taylor Glacier Blood Falls (-77.72°S) mapped in DAXDA's Polar Ice dataset.
mapped_biosignature_sites.earth_analog: Blood Falls Hypersaline Subglacial Reservoir & Lake Vostok (Antarctica)

mapped_biosignature_sites.name: Utopia & Arcadia Planitia — Shallow Subsurface Pure Ice Sheet
mapped_biosignature_sites.mission_and_year: MRO SHARAD Radar / Viking 2 / Zhurong Rover (1976–2024)
key_detections: 80–170 m thick deposit of 50%–85% pure hexagonal water ice (Ih) buried under just 1–10 m of regolith dust
Total water volume (~14,300 km3) exceeds Lake Superior
Polygonal thermal-contraction troughs (60°/120° hexagonal surface fracture networks) and ancient marine sedimentary wedges

host_mineral_crystallography.primary_minerals: Hexagonal Glacial Ice (Ice Ih) + Polygonal Sulfate Crusts
host_mineral_crystallography.lattice_role: Macro-scale 60°/120° hexagonal thermal contraction polygons on the Utopia surface mirror the atomic P6_3/mmc D6h hexagonal unit cell of the underlying water-ice sheet.

mapped_biosignature_sites.planetary_geometric_alignment: Occupies the center of the Utopia Impact Basin (the largest confirmed impact basin in the Solar System, 3,300 km diameter), preserving the frozen remnant of the Northern Oceanus Borealis.
mapped_biosignature_sites.earth_analog: Devon Island / Axel Heiberg Permafrost Polygons (Canadian High Arctic)
